candidates.next_evidence: Track 2026 quarterly disclosures for LEAP deliveries, commercial engine deliveries, internal/external shop visit growth, spare-parts pricing, supply-chain commentary, and airline customer dissatisfaction around delivery or durability.
candidates.node_relation: Second-order scarce supplier to travel capacity: commercial aircraft engines, LEAP engine production, engine services, and MRO turnaround affect airline fleet availability and therefore air-travel capacity.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer travel demand can be capacity-limited by aircraft and engine availability; GE Aerospace benefits if flight hours, engine shop visits, spare parts, and engine deliveries remain elevated.
candidates.why_include: GE Aerospace’s 2025 annual report explicitly discusses constrained aerospace supply chains, material availability, LEAP engine deliveries, engine shop visits, and efforts to reduce MRO turnaround times. This makes GE a high-quality supplier bottleneck candidate for the travel-capacity node.

candidates.next_evidence: Check FY2026 filings for commercial aftermarket organic growth, OEM build-rate exposure, sole-source/proprietary product mix, margin sustainability, leverage risk, and any regulatory or customer pushback on aerospace-part pricing.
candidates.node_relation: Second-order scarce supplier: proprietary aircraft components and aftermarket parts support aircraft utilization, MRO cycles, and fleet uptime.
candidates.theme_relation: If consumer travel demand keeps aircraft utilization high while new-aircraft supply remains constrained, proprietary aftermarket parts suppliers may gain from elevated maintenance demand and pricing power.
candidates.why_include: TransDigm describes itself as a producer of highly engineered, often proprietary aircraft components critical to aircraft operation, with significant commercial aftermarket exposure. That fits a Serenity-style chokepoint screen because certification, qualification, and installed-base specificity can limit substitution.

candidates.next_evidence: Monitor lease-rate factors, aircraft utilization, orderbook delivery delays, purchase commitments, airline credit quality, impairments, and realized gains or losses on aircraft sales.
candidates.node_relation: Capacity infrastructure provider: aircraft lessor with owned, managed, and on-order aircraft and engines; can benefit when airlines need lift but OEM deliveries and fleet availability are constrained.
candidates.theme_relation: Travel demand converts into capacity only if airlines can access aircraft. Leasing companies can be a second-order beneficiary of aircraft scarcity, higher utilization, lease rates, and extended asset lives.
candidates.why_include: AerCap reported a portfolio of roughly 3,500 aircraft, engines, and helicopters owned, managed, or on order as of year-end 2025, and management commentary referenced a structural aircraft shortage driven by delivery delays and maintenance backlogs.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify how material STR/hospitality analytics are to CoStar revenue, whether hotel data demand accelerates around 2026 event markets, and whether this exposure is large enough to matter relative to CoStar’s broader real-estate data business.
candidates.node_relation: Data infrastructure provider for constrained lodging markets through STR hospitality benchmarking, hotel supply/demand data, RevPAR/ADR forecasting, and event-market analytics.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Real estate and hospitality data / analytics
candidates.theme_relation: In event-driven lodging markets, pricing power and capacity signals depend on reliable demand, supply, and benchmarking data. CoStar/STR is a picks-and-shovels exposure to hotel operators, investors, and travel-market forecasters rather than a direct room-supply owner.
candidates.why_include: CoStar’s STR/Tourism Economics hotel forecasts explicitly discuss 2026 RevPAR, ADR, constrained hotel supply growth, and major-event market assumptions, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup impact on individual markets.

candidates.next_evidence: Track passenger volumes by airport, 2026 World Cup or tourism spillover to Guadalajara/Mexico travel corridors, tariff adjustments, capex execution under the 2025-2029 MDP, and regulatory risk.
candidates.node_relation: Regulated travel infrastructure provider: operates airport concessions in Mexico and Jamaica, including Guadalajara, Tijuana, Los Cabos, Puerto Vallarta, and other travel gateways; airport capacity and tariffs are regulated inputs to travel flows.
candidates.theme_relation: Airport concessions can benefit from passenger traffic, tourism flows, cross-border travel, and event-linked demand, while capacity expansion and pricing are constrained by master development plans and regulated maximum tariffs.
candidates.why_include: PAC’s Mexican airport Master Development Program and maximum tariffs for 2025-2029 were approved by Mexican aviation authorities, making it a regulated infrastructure candidate tied to travel capacity rather than an undifferentiated airline operator.

evidence.claim: GE Aerospace reported that 2025 aerospace supply chains remained constrained by material availability, labor shortages, and other obstacles, while total engine deliveries rose 26% year over year and LEAP deliveries rose 28%.
GE Aerospace reported 2025 commercial engine sales of 2,386 units, including 1,802 LEAP engines, and stated that engine deliveries increased primarily due to improved material supply.

TransDigm describes itself as a leading global designer, producer, and supplier of highly engineered aircraft components critical to the safe and effective operation of nearly all commercial and military aircraft.

evidence.source_title: Cruise Ship Orderbook Moves to $90 Billion of New Ships

memory_update.text: GE should be tracked as an aircraft-engine and MRO bottleneck candidate for consumer travel capacity; relevant KPIs include LEAP deliveries, spare parts, shop visits, material availability, and turnaround time.

TDG should be tracked as a proprietary aerospace aftermarket parts candidate; the key Serenity question is whether certification/installed-base specificity creates durable scarcity and pricing power as aircraft utilization remains high.
AER should be tracked as aircraft-capacity infrastructure rather than an airline; aircraft delivery delays and maintenance backlogs can increase the value of owned and leased fleets.
CSGP is a non-obvious data-infrastructure candidate through STR hotel benchmarking and event-market forecasting, but materiality to total CoStar revenue needs further validation.

PAC is a regulated airport-infrastructure candidate tied to tourism, cross-border travel, and possibly event-driven traffic; verify World Cup exposure by airport and route before upgrading confidence.

Cruise shipbuilding is likely a real capacity chokepoint, but the most direct shipyard suppliers are largely non-US-listed; US-listed cruise operators may be covered in a separate direct-capacity pass rather than this scarce-supplier pass.

Sabre is relevant travel-distribution infrastructure, but it was not included in the final five candidates because of market-cap uncertainty and weaker scarcity versus engines, aircraft leasing, regulated airports, and STR hotel data.

node: Travel experiences: cruises, hotels, online travel platforms, airlines, attractions, and event-driven lodging
summary: Expanded universe for scarce or capacity-constrained enablers around travel experiences. The strongest chokepoint-adjacent candidates are not necessarily airlines or hotels themselves, but aircraft engine/parts suppliers, aircraft lessors, regulated airport concessions, hotel market data infrastructure, and travel distribution software. Key bottleneck themes: aircraft delivery and maintenance constraints, proprietary aerospace aftermarket parts, leased-aircraft availability, regulated airport capacity/tariff regimes, hotel supply growth lag, event-market forecasting, and GDS/travel marketplace infrastructure.
